q-sop-02.Perform a water test on suspected leaks: Leaks matter, but the SOP does not ask an inspector to run water over a roof to recreate one.

q-sop-03.Verify each alarm is hardwired and inter: Hardwiring and interconnection run inside walls and ceilings. Ask whether an inspector could confirm either without opening up the building.

q-sop-04.Acceptable, because the test button soun: A sounding horn feels like a clean pass. Ask whether a working horn tells you anything about how old the alarm is.
q-sop-04.Not reportable, since alarm age is outsi: SOP limits set what you must check, not what you may write. Ask whether a limit like that makes anything unreportable.

q-sop-05.In the hallway outside the bedrooms and: That pattern matches an older rule. Ask whether a hallway alarm alone protects someone asleep behind a closed door.

q-sop-06.A basement, a crawlspace, or an open-air: Below-grade spaces and carports describe the home's layout. Ask whether NC ties this duty to layout or to equipment.
q-sop-06.Bedrooms on more than one story, or a fi: Bedroom-by-story wording borrows from smoke alarm placement. Ask whether the NC carbon monoxide list follows that same placement logic.
q-sop-06.An electric furnace, a heat pump, or a d: Review 11 NCAC 08 .1110(d)(2) and recall the home features it lists for carbon monoxide alarm reporting.

q-sop-07.Solid wood at least 2 in thick, or a 45-: Heavier and higher-rated sounds safer. Ask whether the course's residential garage rule actually demands a door this heavy.

q-sop-08.A concern when a bedroom opens directly: A bedroom opening onto a garage is a separate issue. Check whether the stem mentions a bedroom at all.

q-sop-10.Thin aluminum duct, with a register to h: Review the course's rule for ducts that pass through the garage-to-house separation, and why that wall matters.

q-sop-14.A six-foot stepladder: Review 11 NCAC 08 .1101(28), the NC definition of a readily openable access panel, and the reach limit it sets.

q-sop-19.200 hours: 80 classroom and 120 field, i: Review rule .1021 and recall both the total hours and how NC divides them between academic and field instruction.

q-sop-21.$1,000,000 general liability, with no bo: A million-dollar policy sounds safe, but recall what G.S. 143-151.58 actually lists instead of a common commercial policy limit.

q-sop-25.Three per floor inside, and two per side: Those counts sound thorough. Ask whether NC measures the sample floor by floor, or by some other unit of the house.

q-sop-28.Building science, Business practices, Re: Those are skills a business needs. Ask whether a licensing exam tests how you run a company.
q-sop-28.Electrical, Plumbing, Mechanical, and St: Structural pest control is a separately licensed trade in NC. Ask whether the home inspector exam would test another profession's field.

q-sop-29.Describe, Diagnose, Implication, Disclos: Inspectors are careful not to claim they diagnose causes. Ask whether the step after Describe would use that word.

q-sop-30.Yes, NC requires the garage-to-house doo: A blanket yes assumes NC copied the national sentence word for word. Ask whether NC's door rule has conditions or differences.

q-sop-31.No contract, since the house is unoccupi: Ask whether NC ties its pre-inspection requirements to whether anyone lives in the house yet.
q-sop-31.A copy of the building permit and the bu: Permits and builder permission concern the construction site. Ask whether the new NC rule was written about site access.
q-sop-31.A verbal agreement with the builder cove: Agreeing scope and price is sensible. Ask whether the builder is the party you are inspecting for.

q-sop-33.Whether you entered the space, and how l: Time inside sounds like diligence. Ask whether the amended rule measures your effort, or something else about the space.

q-ea-01.Acceptable, as long as both conductors a: Matching gauge sounds tidy. Ask what the breaker's listing says about how many conductors its terminal accepts.

q-ea-02.Each ground needs its own terminal; neut: Same size sounds like a safe condition. Ask whether a matching wire size is enough to let two neutrals share a terminal.

q-ea-03.They ventilate the panel and should be l: Knockouts are made for cable and raceway entry. Ask whether a manufacturer would leave cooling to those holes.
q-ea-03.They are cosmetic, since the dead front: Cosmetic means appearance only. Ask whether an open hole in an electrical enclosure is only about appearance.

q-ea-04.When it is a separate white wire run in: Review the code exception that lets a white conductor serve as a hot, and the conditions it sets.

q-ea-05.The directory should list wire gauge and: Breaker size is already printed on each handle. Ask whether repeating it in the directory fixes these labels.

q-ea-06.The panel's manufacture date and the rec: Brand recalls matter for some panels. Ask whether recall research is part of a visual inspection's required scope.
q-ea-06.Signs of a lightning strike or surge, an: A seller's story is something you cannot confirm. Ask whether a surge history is anything an inspector can verify on site.
q-ea-06.Nothing more; rust inside a panel is cos: Rust inside electrical equipment is more than appearance. Ask whether noting it and moving on fits a panel with corrosion.

q-ea-07.Safety hazard; the aluminum wiring shoul: Replacing wiring throughout goes well past what you saw at the main lugs. Ask how far one observation can stretch.
q-ea-07.Major defect; refer for a derating calcu: A derating calculation is design work. Ask whether an inspector orders one from a look at the lugs.
q-ea-07.Report it as single-strand aluminum bran: Review exactly which aluminum wiring NC SOP .1110(c) names, then decide whether this stem describes it.

q-ea-08.An overloaded circuit; recommend a large: A larger breaker lets more current through the same wire. Ask what that does to the wire's protection.
q-ea-08.A failed breaker that the seller should: Deciding who fixes what before closing is a negotiation call. Ask whether that belongs in an inspector's report.

q-ea-11.It absorbs thermal expansion and contrac: Review the parts of an overhead service entrance, from the service drop to the weatherhead, and what each part is for.

q-ea-13.Equipment ground: Grounded and grounding are different terms. The equipment ground is a grounding conductor, so look past the similar sound.

q-ea-14.Separated, with the neutral bar bonded t: Review the neutral and ground rules for service equipment versus a downstream panel, then compare each option.

q-er-01.Kitchen countertops and bathrooms, by ro: Room names are how older GFCI rules were often taught. Check whether NC .1110 defines its list the same way.
q-er-01.Bathrooms, kitchens, and garages, but no: That list reads like a room checklist. Ask whether NC .1110 builds its list from room names at all.

q-er-03.The receptacle will not power anything u: Reversed means swapped, not disconnected. Ask whether a three-light tester would light at all on a dead receptacle.

q-er-05.Acceptable, because the receptacle still: Power at the slots proves hot and neutral. Ask whether that tells you anything about the third prong.
q-er-05.Correct it yourself with a three-to-two: Inspectors report conditions; the SOP does not ask them to make repairs. Ask whether a field fix belongs in your role.

q-er-06.Reset it, retest once, and mark it accep: Review what a GFCI test button is meant to show, and how the NC SOP expects you to handle the result.

q-er-09.It wastes energy; recommend an LED bulb: Energy use is a client preference, not a repair item. Ask what makes a closet fixture reportable in the first place.
q-er-09.Acceptable if the bulb is under 60 watts: Wattage and a pull chain sound like safeguards. Ask whether the course ties closet fixture rules to either one.

q-er-11.Stranded aluminum service entrance condu: Large stranded feeders are common and accepted when properly terminated. Ask whether NC would single them out.

q-er-13.Disposals are plug-in appliances, which: Some disposals do plug in. Ask whether appliance limits in the SOP excuse a wiring connection you can see.
q-er-13.It is a concern if the disposal is noisy: Noise and vibration are about the motor. Ask whether this question is about the motor at all.
q-er-13.It is acceptable when the cable is a fle: Calling it a flexible cord renames the wire. Ask whether renaming it changes the installation rules that apply.

q-ca-02.4-mil polyethylene, with seams butted an: Tape on a butt joint tends to lift in a damp crawlspace. Ask how the code wants the seams joined.

q-ca-03.Recommend a dehumidifier sized for the c: A dehumidifier treats damp air. Ask whether standing water on the soil is the same problem as damp air.

q-ca-05.1 sq ft per 50 sq ft, or 1 per 500 with: More venting sounds safer. Recall the model code's base ratio instead of assuming a tighter ratio is better.

q-ca-06.Identify the insect species in the repor: Species identification goes beyond what the SOP asks of a home inspector. Ask what the SOP says about pests generally.

q-ca-07.It is cosmetic, as long as the insulatio: An intact jacket is only one part of a duct run. Ask whether it covers everything the stem describes.
q-ca-07.Flex duct is designed to rest on the soi: Flex duct is light and easy to lay down. Ask what manufacturers say about supporting it off the ground.

q-ap-01.The range sits unlevel, so the oven bake: Leveling is handled by the range's adjustable feet. Ask whether a cooking complaint makes this a safety question.

q-ap-02.Operating the cooktop burners: Review the exclusions listed in NC SOP .1115, then check each option against that list rather than guessing.
q-ap-02.Operating the range hood: A range hood is built in above the cooktop. Ask whether NC lists built-in kitchen fans among its exclusions.

q-ap-04.Through the drain cycle: Review the exact wording NC SOP .1115 uses for operating an installed dishwasher.
q-ap-04.Through a short rinse cycle: Review the exact wording NC SOP .1115 uses for the dishwasher, including whether it is operated at all.

q-ap-05.Not reportable, since the hood was worki: A working fan is a good sign. Ask whether the client would want to know anything about where this hood sends air.

q-ap-08.Outdoors, through a hood with a fine scr: Review the dryer exhaust standard in the course, including where the duct is allowed to end.

q-ap-10.Required if it is a built-in model: Built-in often means included. Ask whether NC's refrigerator rule turns on how the unit is installed.

q-ef-02.The slope makes the lawn look uneven, wh: Curb appeal is a matter of taste. Ask whether a home inspection reports on how a yard looks.
q-ef-02.Runoff will slowly erode the mulch beds: Mulch beds are landscaping, not part of the building. Ask whether mulch is really the main stake here.

q-ef-05.The crack is cosmetic, but buyers expect: Buyer expectation is not a reason to report. Ask whether the crack affects anything besides looks.
q-ef-05.Cracked vinyl gives off fumes in the sun: Vinyl siding is a common, stable exterior product. Ask whether a crack changes what the panel gives off in sunlight.

q-ef-06.Repair; recommend sealing or replacing t: Review how the course sorts concrete cracks into normal, repair, and safety categories.

q-ef-07.Hairline cracks running across the full: Full-width hairline cracks are common as concrete cures and shrinks. Ask whether that alone makes them a deficiency.
q-ef-07.Oil and rust stains near the garage that: Stains are about appearance. Ask whether a home inspection reports how concrete looks.
q-ef-07.Concrete that has darkened and weathered: Darkening is about appearance. Ask whether color change with age is something the inspection reports.

q-eh-02.Recommend removing the downspout so wate: Without a downspout, the gutter outlet still drops its water in one spot. Ask whether that spreads anything along the eave.
q-eh-02.Not reportable, since the gutter system: A working gutter is only part of roof drainage. Ask whether the SOP's interest stops at the gutter.

q-eh-03.Neither standard lets you mention fogged: Inspection standards rarely ban writing down something visible. Ask whether either SOP contains such a ban.
q-eh-03.NC requires reporting it and recommendin: Check the window exclusions in NC .1113 before giving NC this duty.

q-eh-04.It sits level so water can drain off bot: A level surface lets water sit. Ask whether a flat sill really drains water anywhere.
q-eh-04.It slopes inward toward the sash so rain: Follow rain down that slope. Ask what it meets at the sash, and whether that joint is meant to take water.
q-eh-04.It relies on paint alone, so no sealant: Review the course's description of a well-built window sill, including its slope and its trim details.

q-eh-05.It is excluded, so you leave it out of t: Leaving it out entirely is a strong choice. Ask whether an SOP exclusion actually forbids mentioning something you noticed.

q-eh-06.A direct connection between the hot and: A hot to cold link is a real plumbing fault with its own name. Recall how NC defines a cross connection.
